terms.comment: Any living creature, man included (animal … homō, Cic. Leg. 1.22), but as often the beasts as against man (Lewis & Short). An i-stem: ablative animālī, plural animālia, animālium.

evidence: Cic. Amic. 81: in bēstiīs, volucribus, nantibus, agrestibus, cicuribus, ferīs
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for every creature but man, tame or wild (Lewis & Short); also the wild beast of the arena. Its diminutive bēstiola is a little creature, a bug (Cic. ND 2.123).

evidence: Phaedr. 1 prol. 5–7: quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae
terms.comment: The wild animal, the talking beast of the fables; properly the feminine of ferus, wild.

phrases.latin: alia animālia gradiendō, alia serpendō ad pāstum accēdunt, alia volandō, alia nandō
phrases.english: some animals come to their food walking, some crawling, some flying, some swimming
no animal sleeps more soundly (of the seal)

phrases.latin: Aperīs tū manum tuam, et implēs omne animal benedictiōne.
phrases.english: You open your hand and fill every living thing with blessing (the grace before meals).
Which animal did you like best?

bestia.html: De Vaan 71, s.v. bēstia; the series spelling of the libellī.
